answer: Trust propagates via bounded random walks across an attestation graph: after t steps, transition mass is constrained by mixing and cannot rapidly cross a sparse cut. An adversarial sybil cluster—a grove, island, or oasis—has low conductance, φ(S)=|∂S|/vol(S), so its escape probability remains small. Min-cut and transitivity bounds cap its aggregate voting weight by boundary connectivity, preventing an internally dense sybil region from gaining disproportionate influence.
